description: Assess CI/CD pipeline security by inventorying configurations, scanning for exposed secrets, testing build isolation, reviewing deployment gates, and checking artifact integrity.

steps.description: Inventory all CI/CD pipeline configurations, service accounts, and integration points across the build system.

inputs.name: build-system-access
inputs.desc: Access credentials or read permissions for the CI/CD platform

inputs.name: scope-definition
inputs.desc: Which repositories, pipelines, and environments are in scope

outputs.name: pipeline-inventory
outputs.desc: Catalog of all pipelines, triggers, service accounts, and integrations

outputs.name: access-map
outputs.desc: Map of who and what can trigger, modify, or read each pipeline

process: List all pipeline definitions and their trigger conditions
Enumerate service accounts and their permission scopes
Map integration points with external services (artifact registries, deployment targets, notification channels)
Document environment variable configurations per pipeline

steps.description: Check for secrets exposed in environment variables, build logs, configuration files, and pipeline artifacts.

inputs.name: pipeline-inventory
inputs.desc: Catalog of pipelines and their configurations

inputs.name: build-system-access
inputs.desc: Access to read build logs and configurations

outputs.name: secrets-findings
outputs.desc: List of exposed or poorly protected secrets with locations

outputs.name: secret-management-assessment
outputs.desc: Evaluation of secret storage and rotation practices

process: Scan pipeline configuration files for hardcoded secrets, tokens, and API keys
Review build logs for leaked credentials or sensitive values
Check environment variable masking and secret injection mechanisms
Assess secret rotation policies and practices

steps.description: Test whether one build job can access artifacts, environment, or secrets belonging to another build job.

inputs.name: pipeline-inventory
inputs.desc: Catalog of pipelines and their configurations

inputs.name: secrets-findings
inputs.desc: Known secret locations from the scan phase

outputs.name: isolation-results
outputs.desc: Findings on build-to-build access and shared resource risks

outputs.name: shared-resource-map
outputs.desc: Map of shared runners, caches, volumes, and artifacts across pipelines

process: Test whether shared runners allow cross-build file system access
Check if build caches can be poisoned by one pipeline and consumed by another
Verify that secret scoping prevents cross-pipeline access
Test artifact storage isolation between projects

steps.description: Review deployment permissions, approval gates, and promotion controls across environments.

inputs.name: pipeline-inventory
inputs.desc: Catalog of pipelines and their configurations

outputs.name: gate-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of approval gates, manual reviews, and automated checks

outputs.name: deployment-permission-matrix
outputs.desc: Matrix of who can deploy what to which environment

process: Map the promotion path from build to staging to production
Verify that manual approval gates exist for production deployments
Check whether automated security scans block deployment on failure
Test if deployment permissions follow least-privilege

steps.description: Test for dependency confusion attacks where internal package names can be hijacked from public registries.

inputs.name: pipeline-inventory
inputs.desc: Catalog of pipelines with dependency sources

outputs.name: confusion-findings
outputs.desc: List of packages vulnerable to dependency confusion or typosquatting

outputs.name: registry-config-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of registry priority, scoping, and pinning practices

process: Identify all internal package names and their registries
Check if public registries are searched before private ones
Test whether name squatting on public registries would override internal packages
Review version pinning and lock file practices

steps.description: Test artifact integrity controls including signing, checksums, and provenance verification.

inputs.name: pipeline-inventory
inputs.desc: Catalog of pipelines and artifact outputs

outputs.name: integrity-findings
outputs.desc: Assessment of artifact signing, checksums, and provenance

outputs.name: tamper-resistance-score
outputs.desc: Rating of how resistant the pipeline is to artifact tampering

process: Check whether build artifacts are signed and whether signatures are verified at deployment
Test if checksums are computed and validated for all transferred artifacts
Review provenance metadata (SLSA level, build attestations)
Test whether a modified artifact can pass through the pipeline undetected

steps.description: Compile all CI/CD security findings into a prioritized report with remediation recommendations.

outputs.name: cicd-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete CI/CD pipeline security assessment report

outputs.name: remediation-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized list of fixes with effort estimates

process: Aggregate findings by severity (critical, high, medium, low)
Map each finding to a specific remediation action
Estimate effort and risk for each remediation
Produce the final report with executive summary and technical detail

description: Assess identity provider and SSO security by mapping authentication flows, testing token handling, and evaluating federation trust relationships.

steps.description: Map all authentication flows including SAML, OIDC, and OAuth configurations across the identity provider.

inputs.name: idp-access
inputs.desc: Access to identity provider configuration and documentation

inputs.name: scope-definition
inputs.desc: Which applications and flows are in scope

outputs.name: auth-flow-map
outputs.desc: Diagram and inventory of all authentication flows and their configurations

outputs.name: protocol-inventory
outputs.desc: List of protocols in use with version and configuration details

process: Enumerate all configured applications and their authentication protocols
Map the redirect URIs, scopes, and grant types for each OAuth/OIDC application
Document SAML assertion configurations and attribute mappings
Identify custom authentication policies and conditional access rules

steps.description: Test token handling and session management for weaknesses in issuance, validation, and expiration.

outputs.name: token-findings
outputs.desc: Weaknesses found in token issuance, validation, and storage

outputs.name: session-findings
outputs.desc: Weaknesses found in session lifecycle management

process: Check token expiration times and refresh policies
Test whether tokens can be replayed after logout
Verify that token signatures are validated and algorithms are pinned
Check session fixation and concurrent session handling

steps.description: Test whether the identity provider leaks information about valid usernames through login, registration, or password reset flows.

outputs.name: enumeration-findings
outputs.desc: Endpoints and behaviors that leak account existence

outputs.name: timing-analysis
outputs.desc: Response time differences that may indicate valid vs invalid accounts

process: Test login endpoint responses for valid vs invalid usernames
Check password reset flow for account existence disclosure
Measure response timing differences between valid and invalid accounts
Test registration flow for duplicate account detection messages

steps.description: Test multi-factor authentication for bypass scenarios including downgrade attacks and recovery flow weaknesses.

inputs.name: auth-flow-map
inputs.desc: Map of authentication flows with MFA configurations

outputs.name: mfa-bypass-findings
outputs.desc: MFA bypass paths and downgrade attack results

outputs.name: recovery-flow-findings
outputs.desc: Weaknesses in MFA recovery and backup code flows

process: Test whether MFA can be skipped by manipulating the authentication request
Check if MFA backup codes have adequate entropy and rate limiting
Test recovery flows (SMS, email) for interception or social engineering risk
Verify that MFA enrollment cannot be downgraded or removed without re-authentication

steps.description: Review federation trust relationships between identity providers and relying parties for misconfiguration.

inputs.name: auth-flow-map
inputs.desc: Map of authentication flows and federation configs

inputs.name: protocol-inventory
inputs.desc: List of protocols and their configurations

outputs.name: federation-findings
outputs.desc: Misconfigurations in federation trust relationships

outputs.name: trust-boundary-map
outputs.desc: Map of trust boundaries and their enforcement

process: Review SAML metadata exchange and certificate validation
Check for overly permissive redirect URI patterns in OAuth configurations
Test cross-tenant access controls in multi-tenant environments
Verify that assertion consumers validate issuer and audience claims

steps.description: Test logout and token revocation to verify that sessions and tokens are properly invalidated.

outputs.name: logout-findings
outputs.desc: Gaps in logout and session invalidation

outputs.name: revocation-findings
outputs.desc: Gaps in token revocation and propagation

process: Test single logout across federated applications
Check whether access tokens remain valid after logout
Verify that refresh token revocation propagates to access tokens
Test back-channel logout notification handling

steps.description: Compile identity provider assessment findings into a prioritized security report.

outputs.name: idp-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete identity provider security assessment report

outputs.name: remediation-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized remediation actions

process: Classify findings by attack vector and severity
Map findings to authentication framework security requirements (OWASP ASVS)
Write remediation recommendations with implementation guidance
Produce the final report with risk ratings and an executive summary

description: Audit DNS infrastructure security by enumerating records, testing for zone transfers, checking DNSSEC, and identifying subdomain takeover risks.

steps.description: Enumerate all DNS records and zones for the target domains.

inputs.name: target-domains
inputs.desc: List of domains and subdomains in scope

inputs.name: dns-provider-access
inputs.desc: Access to DNS management console or API if available

outputs.name: dns-record-inventory
outputs.desc: Complete inventory of DNS records by type and zone

outputs.name: zone-list
outputs.desc: List of all DNS zones under management

process: Query all standard record types (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, SRV, NS, SOA) for each domain
Perform subdomain discovery using certificate transparency logs and passive DNS
Document nameserver delegations and zone boundaries
Identify wildcard records and their scope

steps.description: Test whether DNS servers allow unauthorized zone transfers (AXFR/IXFR).

inputs.name: zone-list
inputs.desc: List of DNS zones to test

inputs.name: dns-record-inventory
inputs.desc: Inventory of DNS records including NS records

outputs.name: zone-transfer-results
outputs.desc: Results of zone transfer attempts against each nameserver

outputs.name: exposed-records
outputs.desc: Any records disclosed through successful zone transfers

process: Attempt AXFR against each authoritative nameserver for each zone
Attempt IXFR with a serial number of zero to request full transfer
Document any successful transfers and the records disclosed
Check ACLs on zone transfer permissions

steps.description: Test DNSSEC configuration for proper signing, chain of trust, and key management.

outputs.name: dnssec-assessment
outputs.desc: DNSSEC deployment status and configuration quality per zone

outputs.name: chain-of-trust-results
outputs.desc: Validation results for the DNSSEC chain of trust

process: Check whether DNSSEC is deployed for each zone
Validate the chain of trust from root to each signed zone
Check key sizes, algorithms, and rotation schedules
Test for NSEC vs NSEC3 zone walking exposure

steps.description: Identify dangling DNS records pointing to deprovisioned resources that could enable subdomain takeover.

outputs.name: dangling-records
outputs.desc: DNS records pointing to unclaimed or deprovisioned resources

outputs.name: takeover-risk-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of subdomain takeover feasibility for each dangling record

process: Resolve all CNAME records and check if the target still exists
Check A/AAAA records for IP addresses no longer under the organization's control
Test cloud service endpoints (S3, Azure Blob, GitHub Pages, Heroku) for claimability
Classify each dangling record by takeover difficulty and impact

steps.description: Review access controls on the DNS management platform for unauthorized modification risks.

inputs.name: dns-provider-access
inputs.desc: Access to DNS provider console or API

outputs.name: access-control-findings
outputs.desc: Weaknesses in DNS provider access controls

outputs.name: change-audit-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of DNS change logging and audit capabilities

process: Review who has administrative access to modify DNS records
Check for MFA requirements on DNS management accounts
Test API key and token permissions for overly broad access
Review DNS change audit logging and alerting

steps.description: Check for indicators of DNS tunneling being used for data exfiltration or command and control.

outputs.name: tunneling-indicators
outputs.desc: Indicators of DNS tunneling activity

outputs.name: dns-monitoring-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of DNS query monitoring and anomaly detection capabilities

process: Analyze DNS query logs for high-entropy subdomain patterns
Check for unusually large TXT record queries or responses
Test DNS query rate limiting and response size restrictions
Review DNS monitoring and anomaly detection capabilities

steps.description: Compile DNS security findings into a prioritized report with remediation recommendations.

outputs.name: dns-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete DNS infrastructure security audit report

outputs.name: remediation-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized DNS security remediation actions

process: Rank findings by exploitability and business impact
Map each finding to a specific remediation with implementation steps
Identify quick wins vs long-term infrastructure changes
Produce the final report with technical detail and executive summary

description: Assess email infrastructure security by checking authentication records, testing relay and spoofing controls, and reviewing encryption and access.

steps.description: Check SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configurations for correctness and coverage.

inputs.name: target-domains
inputs.desc: Domains to check for email authentication records

inputs.name: email-system-info
inputs.desc: Known email infrastructure details (MX hosts, sending services)

outputs.name: auth-record-findings
outputs.desc: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configuration issues

outputs.name: sending-source-map
outputs.desc: Map of all authorized sending sources per domain

process: Parse SPF records and check for overly broad includes, too many lookups, and missing sources
Verify DKIM key publication and key strength for each signing domain
Check DMARC policy (none, quarantine, reject), reporting URIs, and alignment settings
Identify third-party sending services not covered by SPF or DKIM

steps.description: Test mail servers for open relay vulnerabilities that would allow unauthorized email sending.

inputs.name: email-system-info
inputs.desc: MX hosts and SMTP server addresses

outputs.name: relay-findings
outputs.desc: Open relay test results for each mail server

outputs.name: smtp-config-findings
outputs.desc: SMTP configuration weaknesses found

process: Attempt relay through each MX host with external sender and recipient addresses
Test SMTP VRFY and EXPN commands for information disclosure
Check for authenticated relay misconfigurations
Test SMTP banner information disclosure

steps.description: Test anti-spoofing controls by sending test messages with forged headers and domains.

outputs.name: spoofing-results
outputs.desc: Results of spoofing tests showing which forgeries succeed

outputs.name: header-analysis
outputs.desc: Analysis of how spoofed messages are marked in headers

process: Send test messages spoofing the target domain from an external server
Test display-name spoofing with legitimate-looking sender names
Check whether DMARC policy is enforced (quarantine or reject) on receiving side
Analyze authentication-results headers on delivered test messages

steps.description: Test email gateway filtering for dangerous attachments and malicious links.

inputs.name: email-system-info
inputs.desc: Email gateway and filtering system details

outputs.name: filter-bypass-findings
outputs.desc: Attachment types and link patterns that bypass filtering

outputs.name: filter-coverage-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of content filtering breadth and depth

process: Send test attachments with various executable formats and archive types
Test password-protected archives and nested container formats
Send messages with obfuscated malicious URLs (URL shorteners, redirects, encoding)
Test macro-enabled document handling and sandboxing

steps.description: Check email encryption in transit including STARTTLS enforcement and MTA-STS configuration.

outputs.name: encryption-findings
outputs.desc: STARTTLS, MTA-STS, and DANE configuration status

outputs.name: downgrade-risk
outputs.desc: Assessment of susceptibility to encryption downgrade attacks

process: Test STARTTLS support and certificate validity on each MX host
Check for MTA-STS policy publication and enforcement mode
Check for DANE TLSA records
Test whether connections fall back to plaintext if STARTTLS fails

steps.description: Review mailbox access controls, delegation settings, and administrative permissions.

inputs.name: email-system-info
inputs.desc: Email platform details and admin access

outputs.name: access-findings
outputs.desc: Mailbox access control weaknesses

outputs.name: delegation-map
outputs.desc: Map of mailbox delegations and shared access

process: Review administrative access to email management consoles
Check mailbox delegation and send-as permissions
Test mail flow rules and transport rules for data leakage risks
Review auto-forwarding rules for unauthorized external forwarding

steps.description: Compile email security assessment findings into a prioritized report.

outputs.name: email-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete email infrastructure security assessment report

outputs.name: remediation-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized email security remediation actions

process: Classify findings by attack category (spoofing, interception, filtering bypass, access control)
Map each finding to a remediation action with difficulty rating
Calculate risk scores combining likelihood and impact
Produce the final report with technical detail and executive summary

description: Review cryptographic implementations across a tech stack by inventorying crypto usage, checking standards compliance, and testing for implementation flaws.

steps.description: Inventory all cryptographic usage across the codebase and infrastructure including algorithms, key sizes, and purposes.

inputs.name: scope-definition
inputs.desc: Which systems and code are in scope for the review

outputs.name: crypto-inventory
outputs.desc: Catalog of all cryptographic operations, algorithms, and key sizes in use

outputs.name: crypto-dependency-list
outputs.desc: List of cryptographic libraries and their versions

process: Search codebase for cryptographic API calls (encryption, hashing, signing, key derivation, random number generation)
Identify TLS/SSL configurations in servers and clients
Catalog key sizes and algorithm choices for each usage
List all cryptographic library dependencies and their versions

steps.description: Check that algorithm and key length choices meet current standards (NIST, OWASP, industry guidelines).

outputs.name: standards-findings
outputs.desc: Algorithms and key sizes that fall below current standards

outputs.name: deprecation-timeline
outputs.desc: Timeline for when currently acceptable choices become deprecated

process: Compare each algorithm choice against NIST SP 800-131A and OWASP recommendations
Flag deprecated algorithms (MD5, SHA-1, DES, 3DES, RC4, RSA-1024)
Check key derivation functions for adequate iteration counts (PBKDF2, bcrypt, Argon2)
Identify algorithms approaching end of recommended life

steps.description: Review the key management lifecycle including generation, storage, distribution, rotation, and destruction.

inputs.name: crypto-inventory
inputs.desc: Inventory of cryptographic usage and keys

outputs.name: key-management-findings
outputs.desc: Weaknesses in key lifecycle management

outputs.name: key-storage-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of how and where cryptographic keys are stored

process: Check key generation for proper random number source usage
Review key storage (HSM, KMS, encrypted files, environment variables, hardcoded)
Check key rotation schedules and procedures
Verify key destruction procedures (zeroization, secure deletion)

steps.description: Test for common cryptographic implementation errors including padding oracle, timing attacks, and weak randomness.

outputs.name: implementation-flaws
outputs.desc: Specific implementation errors found in cryptographic code

outputs.name: exploit-feasibility
outputs.desc: Assessment of whether each flaw is practically exploitable

process: Test CBC-mode implementations for padding oracle vulnerabilities
Measure timing differences in comparison operations (MAC verification, password checking)
Check random number generator seeding and usage patterns
Test for nonce reuse in authenticated encryption (GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305)

steps.description: Review certificate management including issuance, renewal, revocation checking, and trust store configuration.

outputs.name: certificate-findings
outputs.desc: Certificate management weaknesses and misconfigurations

outputs.name: trust-store-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of certificate trust store configuration

process: Check certificate validity, key sizes, and signature algorithms
Review certificate renewal automation and monitoring
Test revocation checking (CRL, OCSP, OCSP stapling) in both servers and clients
Check certificate pinning implementations where applicable

steps.description: Assess the ability to migrate cryptographic algorithms in response to new threats or standards changes.

outputs.name: agility-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of how easily algorithms can be swapped or upgraded

outputs.name: migration-risk-map
outputs.desc: Map of hardcoded algorithm choices vs configurable ones

process: Identify hardcoded algorithm choices vs runtime-configurable selections
Assess data at rest for re-encryption feasibility (volume, format, access patterns)
Check protocol negotiation support for algorithm upgrades
Evaluate post-quantum readiness for asymmetric cryptography

steps.description: Compile cryptographic review findings into a prioritized report with a migration roadmap.

outputs.name: crypto-review-report
outputs.desc: Complete cryptographic implementation review report

outputs.name: migration-roadmap
outputs.desc: Prioritized roadmap for cryptographic upgrades

process: Classify findings by severity and exploitability
Build a phased migration plan (immediate fixes, short-term upgrades, long-term transitions)
Map findings to compliance requirements where applicable
Produce the final report with risk ratings and technical recommendations

description: Test IoT device security by analyzing firmware, testing network interfaces, checking default credentials, and assessing physical debug access.

steps.description: Extract, decompress, and analyze device firmware for embedded secrets, hardcoded credentials, and vulnerable components.

inputs.name: firmware-image
inputs.desc: Firmware binary image (extracted from device or downloaded)

inputs.name: device-documentation
inputs.desc: Available technical documentation for the device

outputs.name: firmware-contents
outputs.desc: Extracted filesystem, binaries, and configuration files

outputs.name: embedded-secrets
outputs.desc: Hardcoded credentials, keys, and sensitive strings found in firmware

process: Identify the firmware format and extract the filesystem (binwalk, dd, vendor tools)
Search for hardcoded passwords, API keys, and private keys
Identify third-party libraries and their versions for CVE matching
Analyze binary configurations for debug flags and development settings left enabled

steps.description: Test network interfaces and protocols exposed by the device for vulnerabilities.

outputs.name: network-findings
outputs.desc: Vulnerabilities found in exposed network services

outputs.name: protocol-map
outputs.desc: Map of all network protocols and ports used by the device

process: Port scan the device to identify all listening services
Test each service for known protocol vulnerabilities
Check for unencrypted protocols (Telnet, HTTP, MQTT without TLS)
Test wireless interfaces (WiFi, Bluetooth, Zigbee, Z-Wave) for pairing and communication weaknesses

steps.description: Test for default, weak, and shared credentials across device management interfaces.

outputs.name: credential-findings
outputs.desc: Default and weak credential access results

outputs.name: auth-mechanism-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of authentication mechanisms on all interfaces

process: Test vendor default credentials on all management interfaces
Check whether credentials found in firmware work on the live device
Test for credential reuse across multiple devices of the same model
Assess password complexity requirements and account lockout policies

steps.description: Test the over-the-air update mechanism for integrity, authentication, and rollback protection.

inputs.name: firmware-contents
inputs.desc: Extracted firmware for update mechanism analysis

inputs.name: network-findings
inputs.desc: Network protocol findings for update channel identification

outputs.name: update-findings
outputs.desc: Weaknesses in the firmware update mechanism

outputs.name: tamper-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of attempting to install a modified firmware update

process: Identify the update server and protocol
Check whether firmware updates are signed and the signature is verified before installation
Attempt to serve a modified firmware update to the device
Test for rollback protection (can an older, vulnerable firmware be reinstalled)

steps.description: Assess physical debug interfaces (JTAG, UART, SWD) for access to the device runtime and stored data.

inputs.name: firmware-contents
inputs.desc: Firmware analysis results for boot process understanding

outputs.name: debug-interface-findings
outputs.desc: Accessible debug interfaces and what they expose

outputs.name: physical-access-risk
outputs.desc: Assessment of what an attacker with physical access can achieve

process: Visually inspect the PCB for debug headers, test points, and labeled interfaces
Probe suspected UART and JTAG connections
Attempt to read flash memory contents through debug interfaces
Check whether secure boot is enabled and debug fuses are blown

steps.description: Review data transmitted and stored by the device for privacy and security concerns.

outputs.name: data-findings
outputs.desc: Data privacy and security issues in transmission and storage

outputs.name: data-flow-map
outputs.desc: Map of what data leaves the device, where it goes, and how it is protected

process: Capture and analyze network traffic to identify data being transmitted
Check whether sensitive data (credentials, personal information, telemetry) is encrypted in transit
Test cloud API endpoints that receive device data for authorization controls
Review on-device data storage for encryption and access controls

steps.description: Compile IoT device security findings into a prioritized report with remediation recommendations.

outputs.name: iot-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete IoT device security assessment report

outputs.name: remediation-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized remediation actions for firmware and hardware issues

process: Classify findings by attack surface (network, physical, firmware, cloud)
Assess each finding against OWASP IoT Top 10 categories
Write remediation recommendations distinguishing firmware fixes from hardware redesigns
Produce the final report with risk ratings and executive summary

description: Audit software supply chain security by inventorying dependencies, scanning for vulnerabilities, verifying integrity, and testing for confusion attacks.

steps.description: Inventory all direct and transitive dependencies across the software stack.

inputs.name: codebase-access
inputs.desc: Access to source code and package manager configurations

inputs.name: scope-definition
inputs.desc: Which repositories, services, and languages are in scope

outputs.name: dependency-tree
outputs.desc: Complete dependency tree with direct and transitive dependencies

outputs.name: dependency-metadata
outputs.desc: Metadata for each dependency (maintainer, last update, license, popularity)

process: Parse lock files and manifests for each package manager in use
Build the full transitive dependency tree
Collect metadata on each dependency (maintainer count, update frequency, download count)
Identify dependencies with single maintainers or low activity

steps.description: Scan all dependencies for known vulnerabilities using CVE databases and advisory feeds.

outputs.name: vulnerability-report
outputs.desc: List of known vulnerabilities by dependency with severity scores

outputs.name: exploit-availability
outputs.desc: Assessment of public exploit availability for each vulnerability

process: Match each dependency version against NVD, GitHub Advisory Database, and OSV
Check for vendor advisories not yet in public databases
Assess whether each vulnerability is reachable from the application code
Determine exploit availability and active exploitation status

steps.description: Verify package integrity through checksums, signatures, and provenance attestations.

inputs.name: codebase-access
inputs.desc: Access to lock files and integrity records

outputs.name: integrity-findings
outputs.desc: Packages with missing or failing integrity verification

outputs.name: provenance-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of provenance attestation coverage

process: Check lock files for integrity hashes and verify them against registry
Test whether package manager verifies signatures on download
Check for Sigstore or other provenance attestations
Identify packages installed from source without integrity verification

steps.description: Assess dependency update practices including automation, review, and response time to security advisories.

outputs.name: update-practice-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of how quickly and thoroughly dependencies are updated

outputs.name: stale-dependencies
outputs.desc: List of dependencies significantly behind their latest versions

process: Measure the lag between dependency security releases and adoption in the codebase
Check for automated dependency update tooling (Dependabot, Renovate)
Review the dependency update review and merge process
Identify dependencies pinned to end-of-life or unsupported versions

steps.description: Test for dependency confusion and typosquatting vulnerabilities in the package resolution chain.

outputs.name: confusion-findings
outputs.desc: Packages vulnerable to dependency confusion or namespace attacks

outputs.name: registry-config-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of registry priority and scoping configuration

process: Identify internal package names and check for public registry availability
Check package manager registry priority configuration
Test for namespace squatting possibilities on public registries
Review scoped vs unscoped package usage patterns

steps.description: Test whether builds are reproducible to detect unauthorized modifications in the build output.

inputs.name: codebase-access
inputs.desc: Access to build configurations and CI pipeline

outputs.name: reproducibility-results
outputs.desc: Results of reproducible build attempts

outputs.name: build-environment-findings
outputs.desc: Factors preventing reproducibility (timestamps, non-determinism)

process: Attempt to rebuild from the same source and dependencies in a clean environment
Compare build outputs byte-for-byte or with diffoscope
Identify sources of non-determinism (timestamps, file ordering, non-pinned tools)
Assess the feasibility of achieving fully reproducible builds

steps.description: Compile supply chain security findings into a prioritized report with a remediation roadmap.

outputs.name: supply-chain-report
outputs.desc: Complete software supply chain security audit report

outputs.name: remediation-roadmap
outputs.desc: Phased roadmap for supply chain security improvements

process: Classify findings by SLSA level and supply chain attack taxonomy
Prioritize by exploitability and blast radius
Build a phased remediation roadmap (immediate patches, tooling adoption, process changes)
Produce the final report with executive summary and technical appendix

description: Run an incident response tabletop exercise by defining a scenario, walking through detection and response procedures, and identifying gaps.

steps.description: Define the incident scenario including attack vector, scope, and injects for the tabletop exercise.

inputs.name: organization-context
inputs.desc: Description of the organization's infrastructure and threat landscape

inputs.name: exercise-objectives
inputs.desc: What the exercise aims to test (detection, escalation, recovery, communication)

outputs.name: scenario-document
outputs.desc: Written scenario with timeline, injects, and expected discussion points

outputs.name: participant-guide
outputs.desc: Guide for participants including roles and ground rules

process: Select the incident type based on the organization's threat profile (ransomware, data breach, insider threat, DDoS)
Write the scenario narrative with a realistic attack chain
Prepare injects (new information revealed at timed intervals during the exercise)
Define success criteria for each phase of the response

steps.description: Walk through how the incident would be detected and initially triaged given current tooling and procedures.

inputs.name: organization-context
inputs.desc: Current detection tools and monitoring capabilities

outputs.name: detection-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of whether and how quickly the incident would be detected

outputs.name: triage-walkthrough
outputs.desc: Step-by-step record of triage decisions and their rationale

process: Identify which monitoring tools or alert rules would fire for this attack
Estimate time to detection based on current coverage
Walk through initial triage steps: severity classification, scope assessment, evidence preservation
Document decisions made and information gaps encountered

steps.description: Test escalation procedures and communication plans including notification chains and external reporting.

outputs.name: escalation-findings
outputs.desc: Gaps and delays found in escalation procedures

outputs.name: communication-findings
outputs.desc: Issues with internal and external communication plans

process: Walk through the escalation chain: who is notified, in what order, by what channel
Test internal communication plans (technical team, management, legal, PR)
Check external notification requirements (regulators, customers, law enforcement)
Identify single points of failure in the notification chain

steps.description: Exercise containment and eradication procedures to stop the attack and remove the attacker's access.

outputs.name: containment-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of containment effectiveness and speed

outputs.name: eradication-gaps
outputs.desc: Gaps in the ability to fully remove the attacker's presence

process: Walk through containment options (isolate hosts, block IPs, disable accounts, segment network)
Assess the blast radius of each containment action (business impact, collateral disruption)
Exercise eradication steps: remove malware, patch the entry point, reset compromised credentials
Check for persistence mechanisms that would survive initial remediation

steps.description: Review recovery procedures and business continuity plans for restoring operations after the incident.

outputs.name: recovery-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of recovery procedure adequacy and timeline

outputs.name: continuity-gaps
outputs.desc: Gaps in business continuity during recovery

process: Walk through system restoration from backups, validating backup integrity
Assess how long each critical service would be down
Test failover and alternate operation procedures
Check evidence preservation during recovery (forensic images before rebuilding)

steps.description: Identify gaps and improvement actions from the entire tabletop exercise.

outputs.name: gap-list
outputs.desc: Prioritized list of gaps identified across all response phases

outputs.name: improvement-actions
outputs.desc: Specific improvement actions with owners and timelines

process: Compile findings from each exercise phase into a unified gap list
Classify gaps by response phase and severity
Define specific improvement actions for each gap
Assign owners and target dates for each action

steps.description: Compile the tabletop exercise results into a final report for leadership and the security team.

outputs.name: tabletop-report
outputs.desc: Complete tabletop exercise report with findings and recommendations

outputs.name: action-tracker
outputs.desc: Trackable list of improvement actions for follow-up

process: Write the exercise summary including scenario, participants, and timeline
Document key decisions made and their outcomes
Present gaps and improvement actions organized by priority
Produce the final report with both executive and technical sections

description: Assess privilege escalation paths by mapping roles and permissions, testing horizontal and vertical escalation, and reviewing permission inheritance.

steps.description: Map all user roles and their associated permissions across the application and infrastructure.

inputs.name: application-access
inputs.desc: Access to the application with accounts at different privilege levels

inputs.name: scope-definition
inputs.desc: Which applications and infrastructure components are in scope

outputs.name: role-permission-matrix
outputs.desc: Matrix of roles to permissions across all application functions

outputs.name: admin-surface-map
outputs.desc: Map of all administrative functions and who can access them

process: Enumerate all defined roles and their documented permissions
Map each role to the actual API endpoints and functions it can access
Identify administrative functions and their access requirements
Document permission inheritance chains (group membership, role nesting)

steps.description: Test for horizontal privilege escalation where one user can access another user's data or actions at the same privilege level.

inputs.name: application-access
inputs.desc: Test accounts at the same privilege level

outputs.name: horizontal-findings
outputs.desc: Instances where one user can access another's data or functions

outputs.name: data-isolation-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of tenant and user data isolation

process: Test accessing resources belonging to another user at the same privilege level
Swap user identifiers in API requests (user IDs, account numbers, object references)
Check for predictable or enumerable resource identifiers
Test multi-tenant isolation boundaries

steps.description: Test for vertical privilege escalation where a lower-privilege user can gain administrative or higher-privilege access.

outputs.name: vertical-findings
outputs.desc: Paths from lower to higher privilege levels

outputs.name: admin-bypass-findings
outputs.desc: Administrative functions accessible without proper authorization

process: Access administrative endpoints with lower-privilege credentials
Test for role parameter manipulation in requests
Check for self-service role elevation mechanisms
Test forced browsing to administrative URLs and API endpoints

steps.description: Check for insecure direct object references that allow accessing resources by manipulating identifiers.

inputs.name: application-access
inputs.desc: Test accounts with known resource ownership

outputs.name: idor-findings
outputs.desc: Endpoints vulnerable to insecure direct object reference

outputs.name: id-scheme-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of identifier predictability and authorization checking

process: Identify all API endpoints that accept object identifiers
Test each endpoint with identifiers belonging to other users or resources
Check whether sequential, UUIDv1, or otherwise predictable identifiers are used
Verify server-side authorization checks on each object access

steps.description: Test whether authentication tokens can be manipulated to elevate privileges.

outputs.name: token-elevation-findings
outputs.desc: Token manipulation techniques that result in privilege elevation

outputs.name: token-validation-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of server-side token validation

process: Inspect JWT tokens for role claims and test modifications (algorithm confusion, claim editing)
Test session token predictability and forgeability
Check for privilege caching issues where a token retains old permissions after role changes
Test OAuth scope elevation by requesting higher scopes than authorized

steps.description: Review permission inheritance chains and delegation paths for unintended privilege accumulation.

outputs.name: inheritance-findings
outputs.desc: Unintended privilege paths through permission inheritance

outputs.name: delegation-findings
outputs.desc: Risky permission delegation patterns

process: Trace permission inheritance from group membership through nested roles
Identify permissions that accumulate through multiple group memberships
Check for delegation chains that bypass normal authorization (service accounts, API keys)
Test for permission persistence after role revocation

steps.description: Compile privilege escalation findings into a prioritized report.

outputs.name: privesc-report
outputs.desc: Complete privilege escalation assessment report

outputs.name: remediation-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized remediation actions for authorization flaws

process: Classify findings by escalation type and impact
Build attack chains showing how individual findings combine for greater impact
Map findings to OWASP access control requirements
Produce the final report with risk ratings, proof-of-concept details, and remediation steps

description: Audit security logging and monitoring by inventorying sources, testing detection rules, and verifying the incident detection pipeline end to end.

steps.description: Inventory all log sources, their coverage of security-relevant events, and their delivery to the central platform.

inputs.name: infrastructure-map
inputs.desc: Map of systems, applications, and network components

inputs.name: siem-access
inputs.desc: Access to the central logging or SIEM platform

outputs.name: source-inventory
outputs.desc: Catalog of all log sources with event types and delivery status

outputs.name: coverage-gaps
outputs.desc: Systems and event types not currently captured in central logging

process: List all systems expected to produce security logs (servers, applications, network devices, cloud services)
Verify that each source is actively delivering logs to the SIEM
Map event types collected per source (authentication, authorization, changes, errors)
Identify gaps where security-relevant events are not being captured

steps.description: Check log integrity protections against tampering, deletion, and unauthorized access.

outputs.name: integrity-findings
outputs.desc: Weaknesses in log integrity and tamper protection

outputs.name: access-control-findings
outputs.desc: Issues with who can read, modify, or delete logs

process: Check for write-once or append-only log storage configurations
Test whether logs can be modified or deleted by administrators
Verify log transmission encryption (TLS for syslog, HTTPS for API-based collection)
Check for tamper detection (hashing, blockchain-style chaining, digital signatures)

steps.description: Test detection and alert rules against known attack patterns to verify they fire correctly.

inputs.name: siem-access
inputs.desc: Access to SIEM rules and alert configurations

inputs.name: source-inventory
inputs.desc: Log source inventory for understanding available data

outputs.name: detection-findings
outputs.desc: Attack patterns that do and do not trigger alerts

outputs.name: rule-coverage-map
outputs.desc: Map of MITRE ATT&CK techniques to existing detection rules

process: Map existing alert rules to MITRE ATT&CK techniques
Execute controlled test scenarios for critical attack techniques (credential dumping, lateral movement, exfiltration)
Verify that expected alerts fire within acceptable time windows
Identify high-priority ATT&CK techniques with no detection coverage

steps.description: Verify that log retention periods meet regulatory and compliance requirements.

inputs.name: infrastructure-map
inputs.desc: Compliance frameworks applicable to the organization

outputs.name: retention-findings
outputs.desc: Log sources not meeting retention requirements

outputs.name: compliance-mapping
outputs.desc: Mapping of log types to applicable retention requirements

process: Identify applicable retention requirements (PCI DSS: 1 year, SOX: 7 years, HIPAA: 6 years, GDPR: varies)
Check actual retention settings for each log source and storage tier
Verify that archived logs are retrievable within required timeframes
Check for conflicts between retention requirements and data minimization obligations

steps.description: Check logs for sensitive data that should not be logged (credentials, PII, health data, payment data).

inputs.name: siem-access
inputs.desc: Access to search and sample log data

outputs.name: sensitive-data-findings
outputs.desc: Instances of sensitive data found in logs

outputs.name: data-handling-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of log sanitization and masking practices

process: Sample logs from each source and scan for common sensitive data patterns (SSN, credit card, email, password)
Check application logs for request/response body logging that may capture credentials
Test whether error messages in logs expose internal system details
Review log masking and redaction configurations

steps.description: Test the incident detection pipeline end to end from event generation to analyst notification.

outputs.name: pipeline-assessment
outputs.desc: End-to-end assessment of detection pipeline reliability and speed

outputs.name: bottleneck-analysis
outputs.desc: Identified bottlenecks in the detection and notification chain

process: Generate a controlled security event and measure time from event to log ingestion
Measure time from ingestion to alert rule evaluation and firing
Measure time from alert to analyst notification through the configured channels
Test pipeline behavior under load to identify ingestion lag or dropped events

steps.description: Compile logging and monitoring audit findings into a prioritized report.

outputs.name: logmon-audit-report
outputs.desc: Complete logging and monitoring security audit report

outputs.name: remediation-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized improvements for detection capability

process: Classify findings by impact on detection capability and compliance
Map detection gaps to MITRE ATT&CK to show where the organization is blind
Build a phased improvement plan (quick coverage wins, rule tuning, infrastructure changes)
Produce the final report with executive summary and technical appendix
